description: Cross-language golden fixture for S2 signal emission (INT-3, #1394 S2 aligned). Single source of truth for the 14-event list: the Go side keeps an in-code emitter table (F8 precedent, task-transitions.json) and cross-checks it against this file in tests; the Python side reads this file at runtime. Precedent: task-transitions.json.
id_rule: event_id = 'ev_' + sha256(team_id|project_id|task_id|loop_id|event_type|source_event|iteration|fingerprint|attempt|audit_seq)[:16] hex. Fixed field order; each field is a plain string, empty string when the emitter carries no such identity (project-level events leave task_id empty; task events set project_id and leave loop_id/iteration empty; iteration is the decimal iteration_index or empty). fingerprint = the event fingerprint field = hex(sha256 of the ref bytes after the main write) - the stable identity of the logical operation's result. audit_seq = the project's persisted committed-operation revision (project meta 'audit_seq'; 0 when absent): advanced by exactly one on each committed Go intervention write (markAuditFields + conditional ETag write), it is the persistent identity of the operation INSTANCE. A retry of the same operation re-reads the same committed revision and the same state bytes, so it re-lands on the same id (consumers dedupe by event_id, keyed on the operation identity per #1394), while two distinct operations - another project, another loop iteration, or a second occurrence of the same control operation (pause/resume/pause within one wall-clock second, whose post-write state bytes are byte-identical at second-precision updated_at) - hash distinct inputs and cannot share a key. No raw timestamp is ever part of the identity; audit_seq, not the clock, distinguishes operation instances. Rejection family (SIG-MISMATCH): a rejection commits no state, so the ref bytes - and the fingerprint - are identical across distinct rejected operations on the same task state; those emitters append one extra final component `action|from|to` (the rejection discriminator) to the hash input. Distinct rejections therefore get distinct ids, while a retry of the same rejection re-hashes identically. Events without a discriminator hash the fixed ten-field input above unchanged (the cross-language fixed vector is unaffected; Go has no rejection emitter).
source_event_note: source_event = the row's row id, unique per emit point. It is hashed into id_rule, so two emit points must never share it (11-SIGNAL: submit and accept share source_event.origin=submit but use different source_events to keep ids distinct).
